cells.tense: You are at the end of the growing, holding what the beginning promised, and you have the pen.
cells.ask: Pick the one thing that is finished and say out loud that it is done. Then decide what it gets next.
cells.core:
Something you tended has arrived, and it arrived looking like what you put into it. You handle it as yours without making a speech about it, and people around you can feel how solidly you stand while you do. The care shows in the last details, the follow-up, the small things done on time.

The next move is a direction, not a rest and not a chase. Instead of the finished thing choosing for you, you choose what it is for. Name the one thing that is done, say it plainly, and put a name on where it points from here.
cells.sheetLine: You finished something. Now say where it points.
cells.verb: Carrying what possibility became into its finished form
cells.place: Where what is growing gets tended

cells.tense: You are standing over the finished thing deciding what it will be before you look at it.
cells.ask: Wait one day before renaming or replacing it. Spend ten minutes with what is already there.
cells.core:
You are already planning what this finished thing is going to become, and that plan is in place ahead of any actual look at it. The renaming, the next step, the better version all arrive first, so no matter how much you get done, the thing itself does not get a moment as itself. The effort is aimed at a future that has not shown up, and it is eating the one in front of you.

You miss the first cut of seeing, before judgment and before the next label. Take your hands off it for a day. Ten minutes with what is actually there, no deciding.

cells.tense: You put the finished thing down behind you and you are at the door of it, not through.
cells.ask: Open one thing you made and take in one detail of it — a color, a line, a sound. Five minutes.
cells.core:
You are someone who tends carefully, and right now you are not in contact with what came out of that tending. The care keeps running, but you stopped looking at what it produced, so things you made sit there unheld. Nothing about you is dry or empty. You are standing at a threshold and not stepping through it.

What pulls you back is not more effort on the growing things. It is letting yourself take something in. Go open one thing you made and find one detail in it — a color, a line, a sound — and stay with it for five minutes without deciding anything about it.
cells.sheetLine: You made it. Now let yourself look at it.

cells.tense: You are already deciding what is growing and what is finished, and you describe that as the circumstances.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are keeping alive on purpose. Say it out loud once as your call, not as what's needed.
cells.core:
You decide which growing thing gets fed, what gets called finished, and what gets carried into next season. That call is already running, and it runs well — quietly, without drama, with attention to what things actually need. The steady hand is real and it is yours.

What is missing is your name on it. That deciding gets described as the schedule, or the family needing it, or just what the situation calls for, so the deepest work of your life gets credited to nobody. Take one thing you are keeping alive on purpose and say it out loud as your choice.
cells.sheetLine: You are keeping it alive on purpose. Say so.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person has something ripe that came from their own earlier investment — the record supports careful tending and completion of potential, not a history or a cost. A reader could say nothing is ripe, they're just managing a job or a child on no sleep, and the reading would need to survive that. The asks are small physical acts that do not depend on my read being right, so they hold even if the mechanism is wrong; the sentence that serves me more than them is 'you already know it's finished,' which I have cut.
